source_read: Papa's Fish & Chips nutritional information page https://papasfishandchips.com/nutritional-information/ (fetched 2026-10-12; still links the six Campden BRI lab-report PDFs and still shows the calculator and 'Regular Haddock & Chips is only 575 kcal per portion'); the six PDFs in /wp-content/uploads/2018/12/ re-downloaded 2026-10-12 with SHA-256 identical to the files first read on 2026-10-09 (Haddock ea74f133, Sausage f3f0385b, Fishcake 1a64e050, Chips cb18a142, Pattie a63faf1b, Mushy Peas 288af6a6); find-us page https://papasfishandchips.com/find-us/ lists 5 restaurants (Blackpool, Cleethorpes, Hull (Willerby), Scarborough, Sheffield)
not_verifiable: whether the December 2018 lab figures still match today's recipes (the chain publishes nothing newer; note.txt gives the date); the fishcake's sodium (printed under 'mg' as 1.35) is left blank
notes: Second read by another reader and method: each PDF rendered with pdftoppm at 110 dpi and every per-portion cell (kJ, kcal, fat, carbohydrate, protein, total sodium) and the printed portion weight read by eye from the image, then compared with items.csv: 6 of 6 tables, 0 differences (Mushy Peas also matches but stays held back). Independent cross-check from the chain's own page: the calculator's kcal for Haddock 217, Battered Sausage 174, Fishcake 212, Pattie 203 and Chips 358 equal the reports' per-portion kcal; its Peas 114 is the report's per-100 g figure, not its 198 kcal per portion, so Mushy Peas stays held back (two official figures disagree). The extraction script also re-checks per-portion = per-100 g x portion weight, kJ about 4.184 x kcal and 4P+4C+9F within 5% for every published row.
